result:
None of the three solutions is correct, as far as I can verify.

**Solution 1 (1/2)** fails the boundary condition. Its pattern places holes at (0,0), (1,1), (2,2) mod 3, so the holes at (0,0) and (1,1) share a corner point. Their boundaries then intersect, which the problem forbids. The argument only checked orthogonal adjacency.

**Solution 2 (3/8)** is also invalid. Its count assumes some cells of the odd-odd class can be left out of P. Any such cell would be an isolated one-cell hole touching the even-even holes at corners, which violates the boundary condition. So the claimed construction does not satisfy the hypotheses.

**Solution 3 (1/4)** rests on Lemma 1, which is false. Two holes on opposite sides of one polyomino square have disjoint boundaries, because the two edges of that square do not meet. The upper bound h_n ≤ n/4 therefore does not follow, and the construction only gives a lower bound.

A valid construction gives a lower bound of 1/3. Take holes at all points (2i, 2j) and put every other cell into P. The holes are single cells whose boundaries are pairwise disjoint and lie in the interior of P. P is connected, and each hole has density 1/4 among grid cells, so h/n → (1/4)/(3/4) = 1/3. This is strictly larger than 1/4, so Solution 3's answer is too small. I did not complete a matching upper bound for general (non-unit) holes, so I cannot rule out a value above 1/3, but none of the three proposed values is supported.

CHOICE: NONE
